For p>=0 positive weights are subharmonic (or constant), and for 2-n<=p<0 spherical potential Gp decreases in offset, making E increase. For subcritical 1-n<p<2-n, p<0, Gp prime is negative for t>1 while a positive-source Poisson identity for t<1 yields Gp prime asymptotic (1-t)^(q-1) blowing up; hence E increases up to r=a and decreases just afterwards, while E~omega r^q at infinity. Rescaled polar-cap difference integral has convergent beta value Gamma(n/2)Gamma(1-q/2)/(sqrt(pi) q Gamma(-p/2)); r^q and (1-a/r)^q cancel offset exactly. Independent exact three-dimensional formula checks at p=-3/2 and p=-5/4 converge two-sided to C=1 and C=2/3. Newtonian p=2-n reduces to shell theorem.
